newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hongkong Bank NZ H1 profit up 50 percent - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank NZ H1 profit up 50 percent - NZPA.

text.p: Hongkong Bank New Zealand, a branch of Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp, on Tuesday reported a sharply higher interim after tax profit of NZ$9.5 million, the New Zealand Press Association reported.

Chief executive John Blanthorne was quotedd as saying the performance for the six months to June 30, up 50 percent on the same period last year, was a good one considering the competitive market conditions during the period.

"While there was continued business growth across all sectors of operations, we have been particularly pleased with the improved earnings for the half year from our treasury and corporate banking operations," Blanthorne said.

He said the bank had continued to build its personal banking business and this had resulted in an annualised growth in mortgages of 90 percent in the period while customer deposits had grown 70 percent.
The bank's assets in new Zealand stood at $3.9 million at June 30.
Overnight the parent HSBC Holdings reported an interim pre-tax profit of 2.62 billion pounds ($NZ6.66 billion), up 13 percent on the same period last year.
